title: What does Pratap do?
scope: The imperfective present (बोलता है, बोलती हैं), dropping the auxiliary in negatives (नहीं बोलतीं); आना for knowing a language; X को क्या कहते हैं ?; होता है for general truths; मालूम होता है; mixed-gender agreement; कितने बजे; X साल का; possessive pronouns तेरा, इसका, हमारा, किनका, अपना, compound postpositions (के लिए, की तरफ़, मेरे साथ …)

vocab.en: Munna (pet name for a little boy)

items.q: Fill the gap: “My sister works in London.”
items.hi: मेरी बहिन लंदन में काम ___ है ।
items.say: मेरी बहिन लंदन में काम करती है ।
wrong: करता
करता is masculine. बहिन is feminine, so the participle is करती.
करतीं
The nasal -tī̃ appears only when हैं is dropped after नहीं. With हैं present, the feminine participle is -tī.
items.why: The participle agrees with the subject: masculine -tā, feminine -tī.

items.q: Fill the gap: “I drink tea in the morning. (a man speaking)”
items.say: मैं सुबह चाय पीता हूँ ।
items.en: I[0] drink[3+4] tea[2] {in the morning}[1]. (a man speaking)
wrong: पीती
पीती is feminine. The speaker is a man.
पीते
-te is masculine plural, for हम, तुम, आप and plural subjects. मैं takes -tā.
items.why: मैं पीता हूँ for a man, मैं पीती हूँ for a woman.

items.q: Fill the gap: “What do you read at night?”
items.say: तुम रात को क्या पढ़ते हो ?
wrong: हैं goes with हम, आप, ये, वे and plural nouns. तुम takes हो.
है
है goes with तू, यह and वह. तुम takes हो.
items.why: The participle is followed by the present of होना, as in तुम पढ़ते हो.

items.q: Fill the gap: “We speak Panjabi at home.”
items.say: हम घर पर पंजाबी बोलते हैं ।
wrong: बोलता
बोलता is singular. हम is plural, so the masculine participle is बोलते.
बोलना
बोलना is the infinitive. The tense uses the participle, stem + -tā, -tī, -te.
items.why: हम takes the -te participle and हैं (a group of women would say बोलती हैं).

items.q: Fill the gap: “Mother gets up early in the morning.”
items.say: माँ जी सुबह जल्दी उठती हैं ।
wrong: उठते
उठते is masculine. Respect makes the verb plural, but माँ is feminine: उठती हैं.
उठतीं
The nasal -tī̃ appears only when हैं is dropped after नहीं. With हैं present, the feminine participle is -tī.
items.why: A respected woman takes the feminine participle with हैं.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Mohan ji knows Hindi and Sanskrit.”
items.hi: मोहन जी हिन्दी और संस्कृत ___ हैं ।
items.say: मोहन जी हिन्दी और संस्कृत जानते हैं ।
wrong: जानता
जानता is for one man spoken of plainly. जी shows respect, so the verb is plural: जानते हैं.
जानती
जानती is feminine. Mohan is a man.
items.why: Respect takes plural agreement, as with है and हैं in unit 1.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Those girls laugh a lot.”
items.say: वे लड़कियाँ बहुत हँसती हैं ।
wrong: हँसते
हँसते is masculine. लड़कियाँ are feminine.
हँसतीं
The nasal -tī̃ appears only when हैं is dropped after नहीं. With हैं present, the feminine participle is -tī.
items.why: Feminine plural: -tī with हैं.

items.q: Change the subject to मेरी बहिनें
wrong: मेरी बहिनें संस्कृत सीखतीं हैं ।
The nasal -tī̃ appears only when हैं is dropped after नहीं. With हैं present, the feminine participle is -tī.
मेरी बहिनें संस्कृत सीखते हैं ।
सीखते is masculine. बहिनें are feminine.
items.why: Feminine plural: the participle is सीखती and the auxiliary हैं.
items.say: मेरी बहिनें संस्कृत सीखती हैं ।

items.q: Fill the gap: “The children play in the garden.”
items.say: बच्चे बग़ीचे में खेलते हैं ।
wrong: खेलता
खेलता is singular. बच्चे is plural.
खेलना
खेलना is the infinitive. A statement uses the participle.
items.why: Masculine plural: -te with हैं.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Which office do you work in? (to a man)”
items.hi: आप किस दफ़्तर में काम ___ हैं ?
items.say: आप किस दफ़्तर में काम करते हैं ?
items.en: {Which office}[1+2] do[6] you[0] work[4+5] in[3]? (to a man)
wrong: करता
करता is singular. आप always takes plural agreement.
करो
करो is the तुम command, not a statement.
items.why: आप takes -te (or -tī for a woman) with हैं.

items.q: Fill the gap: “I sleep very little. (a woman speaking)”
items.say: मैं बहुत कम सोती हूँ ।
wrong: सोता
सोता is masculine. The speaker is a woman.
सोना
सोना is the infinitive (and also the noun “gold”). The tense uses the participle.
items.why: सोना “to sleep”: stem so-, participle सोता, सोती, सोते.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Mohan doesn't go to the office.”
items.say: मोहन दफ़्तर नहीं जाता ।
wrong: जाते
जाते is plural. Mohan, spoken of plainly, is one person.
जातीं
जातीं is the feminine plural form used when हैं is dropped. Mohan is a man.
items.why: In a negative sentence the auxiliary can be dropped: मोहन दफ़्तर नहीं जाता ।

items.q: Fill the gap: “My daughters don't go to school.”
items.say: मेरी बेटियाँ स्कूल नहीं जातीं ।
wrong: जाती
With हैं dropped, the feminine plural participle takes over its nasal: जातीं.
जाते
जाते is masculine. बेटियाँ are feminine.
items.why: Without the auxiliary, a feminine plural participle is nasalized to make up for the lost हैं.

items.q: Make this sentence negative
items.a: सीता शुक्रवार को बाज़ार नहीं जाती ।
wrong: सीता शुक्रवार को बाज़ार नहीं जातीं ।
जातीं is for feminine plural subjects. सीता is one person.
सीता शुक्रवार को बाज़ार मत जाती ।
मत is only for commands. Statements are made negative with नहीं.
items.why: नहीं goes before the verb, and है can be dropped.
items.hi: सीता शुक्रवार को बाज़ार जाती है ।
items.say: सीता शुक्रवार को बाज़ार नहीं जाती ।
items.en: Sita[0] doesn't[4] go[5] {to the market}[3] {on Fridays}[1+2].

items.q: Why does बोलतीं have a nasal here?
items.a: हैं has been dropped, and the feminine plural participle takes its nasal
wrong: Every participle after नहीं is nasalized
Only the feminine plural one is. The masculine plural stays बोलते, वे नहीं बोलते.
लड़कियाँ ends in a nasal, so the verb copies it
The nasal makes up for the dropped हैं. It has nothing to do with the noun's ending.
items.why: With हैं it is बोलती हैं, and without it नहीं बोलतीं.
items.say: ये लड़कियाँ पंजाबी नहीं बोलतीं ।

items.q: Fill the gap: “These boys never laugh in class.”
items.hi: ये लड़के क्लास में कभी नहीं ___ ।
items.say: ये लड़के क्लास में कभी नहीं हँसते ।
items.en: These[0] boys[1] never[4+5] laugh[6] in[3] class[2].
wrong: हँसतें
Not a word: only the feminine plural participle takes a nasal when हैं is dropped.
हँसता
हँसता is singular. लड़के is plural.
items.why: कभी नहीं “never”; the masculine plural stays हँसते without हैं.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Papa sometimes brings samosas.”
items.say: पापा कभी कभी समोसे लाते हैं ।
wrong: कभी नहीं
कभी नहीं means “never”.
हमेशा
हमेशा means “always”.
items.why: कभी कभी “sometimes”, कभी नहीं “never”.

items.q: Make this sentence negative
wrong: मेरी सहेलियाँ उर्दू नहीं समझती ।
With हैं dropped, the feminine plural participle must carry the nasal: समझतीं.
मेरी सहेलियाँ उर्दू मत समझतीं ।
मत is only for commands. Statements are made negative with नहीं.
items.why: Feminine plural without हैं gives नहीं समझतीं.
items.say: मेरी सहेलियाँ उर्दू नहीं समझतीं ।
items.en: My[0] friends[1] don't[3] understand[4] Urdu[2]. (a girl speaking)

lessons.title: आती है, होता है
lessons.desc: Languages, names, general truths, time and age

items.q: Fill the gap: “My wife knows Gujarati.”
items.say: मेरी पत्नी को गुजराती आती है ।
wrong: आता
The verb agrees with the language, गुजराती, which is feminine.
जानती
जानना needs the knower as subject (मेरी पत्नी गुजराती जानती है). With को the verb is आना.
items.why: Knowing a language: X को (language) आना, literally “Gujarati comes to my wife”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “He doesn't know Hindi at all.”
items.say: उसे हिन्दी बिलकुल नहीं आती ।
wrong: वह
With आना the person who knows takes को, giving उस को or उसे.
उसका
उसका means “his”. The knower takes को.
items.why: उसे (= उस को) … आती. Hindi “comes to” him.

items.q: Fill the gap: “People call him a devil.”
items.say: लोग उसे शैतान कहते हैं ।
wrong: कहता
कहता is singular. लोग is plural.
बोलते
बोलना is “to speak”. To call someone something is कहना.
items.why: X को Y कहना “to call X Y”; X को क्या कहते हैं ? asks what X is called.

items.q: Fill the gap: “In the mountains the air is cold.”
items.say: पहाड़ों पर हवा ठंडी होती है ।
items.en: {In the mountains}[0+1] the air[2] is[4+5] cold[3].
wrong: होता
होता is masculine. हवा is feminine.
होते
होते is masculine plural. हवा is feminine singular.
items.why: होता है states what is generally true; है alone describes one particular case.

items.q: Which means “I know that the shop is closed today”?
items.a: मुझे मालूम है कि आज दुकान बंद है ।
wrong: मालूम होता है कि आज दुकान बंद है ।
मालूम होता है means “it seems”.
मैं मालूम हूँ कि आज दुकान बंद है ।
मालूम takes the को construction: मुझे मालूम है.
items.why: मुझे मालूम है “I know”; मालूम होता है “it seems”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Mohan and Sita learn Hindi.”
items.say: मोहन और सीता हिन्दी सीखते हैं ।
wrong: सीखती
When the subjects are people of both sexes the verb is masculine plural. The nearest-word rule is only for things.
सीखता
सीखता is singular. There are two people.
items.why: A man and a woman together take the masculine plural.

items.q: Fill the gap: “In this shop the chairs and beds are old.”
items.hi: इस दुकान में कुरसियाँ और पलंग ___ हैं ।
items.say: इस दुकान में कुरसियाँ और पलंग पुराने हैं ।
items.en: In[2] this[0] shop[1] the chairs[3] and[4] beds[5] are[7] old[6].
wrong: पुरानी
For things of mixed gender, agreement follows the nearest one: पलंग, masculine plural.
पुराना
पुराना is singular. There are several things.
items.why: With things, the gender of the nearest item decides; the verb follows the same rule.

items.q: Fill the gap: “What time does the bus come?”
items.say: बस कितने बजे आती है ?
wrong: साल
साल means “year”. Clock time is बजे.
दिन
दिन means “day”. Clock time is बजे.
items.why: कितने बजे ? “at what time?”; सात बजे “at seven o'clock”.

items.q: Someone about to leave says “अच्छा, मैं चलता हूँ ।”. What does it mean?
wrong: I walk well.
अच्छा at the start is “well then”, not “proficiently”.
I often go for walks.
The imperfective is usually habitual, but here it is an idiom for leaving now.
items.why: The imperfective is used idiomatically for something about to happen: मैं चलता हूँ “I'm off”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “My son is ten years old.”
items.say: मेरा बेटा दस साल का है ।
items.en: My[0] son[1] is[5] ten[2] years[3] old[4].
wrong: की
की is feminine. का agrees with the subject, बेटा.
के
के would be for a plural or respected subject. बेटा is one boy.
items.why: In X साल का “X years old”, का agrees with the person.

items.q: In मेरा बेटा दस साल का है, why is साल not in the oblique plural?
items.a: The ten years make one block of time, not separate years
wrong: The word for “year” has no plural
It does: सालों is its oblique plural, used when years are counted one by one.
The postposition after it does not make it oblique
It does: का is a postposition. Here the years are taken as a single block.
items.why: The same idea gives दस दिन में “in ten days”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Is this your book? (to तू)”
items.say: क्या यह तेरी किताब है ?
wrong: तेरा
तेरा is masculine. किताब is feminine.
तुम्हारी
तुम्हारी goes with तुम. With तू the possessive is तेरा.
items.why: तू gives तेरा, तेरी, तेरे.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Her children are very clever. (a woman nearby)”
items.say: इसके बच्चे बहुत होशियार हैं ।
items.en: Her[0] children[1] are[4] very[2] clever[3]. (a woman nearby)
wrong: इसकी
The possessive agrees with the thing possessed, बच्चे, not with the owner. Her being a woman makes no difference.
इसका
इसका is singular. बच्चे is plural.
items.why: इसका “his, her (of this one)” agrees like an -ā adjective.

items.q: Which asks “whose?” about several owners?
wrong: किसका
किसका asks about a single owner.
कौनसा
कौनसा means “which?”.
items.why: किन is the plural oblique of कौन, so किन + का.

items.q: Fill the gap: “There are two windows in our room.”
items.say: हमारे कमरे में दो खिड़कियाँ हैं ।
items.en: {There are}[5] two[3] windows[4] in[2] our[0] room[1].
wrong: हमारा
कमरे is oblique before में, so हमारा becomes हमारे too.
हमारी
हमारी is feminine. कमरा is masculine.
items.why: A possessive agrees with its noun in case as well: हमारे कमरे में.

items.q: Which means “This bicycle is mine”?
wrong: यह मेरी साइकिल है ।
This means “This is my bicycle”. Before the noun the possessive just describes it.
यह साइकिल मेरा है ।
मेरा is masculine. साइकिल is feminine.
items.why: After the noun, the possessive is what the sentence says about it: “is mine”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Our grandmother is very old.”
items.say: हमारी दादी जी बहुत बूढ़ी हैं ।
wrong: हमारे
Respect makes a masculine possessive plural (हमारे पिता जी), but a feminine one stays हमारी.
हमारा
हमारा is masculine. दादी is feminine.
items.why: हमारा “our” agrees with दादी.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Prakash ji is here; this is his son.”
items.hi: प्रकाश जी यहाँ हैं, यह ___ बेटा है ।
items.say: प्रकाश जी यहाँ हैं, यह इनका बेटा है ।
items.en: {Prakash ji}[0+1] is[3] here[2]; this[4] is[7] his[5] son[6].
wrong: इसका
इसका is for someone spoken of plainly. प्रकाश जी is respected, so the plural इनका.
इनके
इनके is plural or oblique. बेटा is singular and direct.
items.why: A respected person is referred to in the plural: इनका, उनका.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Sita goes to the market with her (own) brother.”
items.hi: सीता ___ भाई के साथ बाज़ार जाती है ।
items.say: सीता अपने भाई के साथ बाज़ार जाती है ।
items.en: Sita[0] goes[6+7] {to the market}[5] with[3+4] {her (own)}[1] brother[2].
wrong: उसके
उसके would mean someone else's brother. When the owner is the subject of the clause, Hindi uses अपना instead.
अपनी
अपना agrees with भाई, which is masculine and oblique before के साथ, not with Sita.
items.why: अपना refers back to the subject and agrees with the thing possessed.

items.q: Fill the gap: “I wash my clothes.”
items.say: मैं अपने कपड़े धोता हूँ ।
wrong: मेरे
The owner is मैं, the subject. When the owner is the subject of the clause, Hindi uses अपना instead.
अपना
अपना is singular. कपड़े is plural.
items.why: “My” referring back to मैं is अपना.

items.q: Fill the gap: “You put your shoes here.”
items.say: तुम अपने जूते यहाँ रखो ।
wrong: तुम्हारे
In a command “your” is always अपना, because the subject of a command is “you”.
अपनी
अपनी is feminine. जूते is masculine plural.
items.why: Commands always take अपना for “your”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “My sister and I learn Hindi. (a man speaking)”
items.hi: मैं और ___ बहिन हिन्दी सीखते हैं ।
items.say: मैं और मेरी बहिन हिन्दी सीखते हैं ।
items.en: My[2] sister[3] and[1] I[0] learn[5+6] Hindi[4]. (a man speaking)
wrong: अपनी
मैं और मेरी बहिन is a joint subject. अपना refers back to a subject; it cannot be part of one.
मेरा
मेरा is masculine. बहिन is feminine.
items.why: In a joint subject joined by और the ordinary possessive is used.

items.q: Fill the gap: “My brother works in the post office.”
items.hi: ___ भाई डाकघर में काम करता है ।
items.say: मेरा भाई डाकघर में काम करता है ।
items.en: My[0] brother[1] works[4+5+6] in[3] {the post office}[2].
wrong: अपना
भाई is itself the subject, so there is nothing for अपना to refer back to.
मेरी
मेरी is feminine. भाई is masculine.
items.why: अपना never goes with the subject itself.

items.q: Which says that Mohan reads his own newspaper?
wrong: मोहन उसका अख़बार पढ़ता है ।
उसका here means someone else's newspaper. When the owner is the subject of the clause, Hindi uses अपना instead.
मोहन अपनी अख़बार पढ़ता है ।
अख़बार is masculine, so it is अपना.
items.why: अपना points back to the subject, Mohan.

items.q: Fill the gap: “These are my very own clothes.”
items.say: ये मेरे अपने कपड़े हैं ।
wrong: अपना
अपना is singular. कपड़े is plural.
अपनी
अपनी is feminine. कपड़े is masculine.
items.why: A possessive followed by अपना is emphatic: “my very own”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “They love their (own) grandmother very much.”
items.hi: वे ___ दादी जी से बहुत प्यार करते हैं ।
items.say: वे अपनी दादी जी से बहुत प्यार करते हैं ।
wrong: उनकी
उनकी would mean someone else's grandmother. When the owner is the subject of the clause, Hindi uses अपना instead.
अपने
Respect makes masculine forms plural, but दादी is feminine: अपनी.
items.why: प्यार करना “to love” marks the person loved with से or को.

items.q: When does Hindi use अपना instead of मेरा, उसका and so on?
items.a: When the owner is the subject of the same clause
wrong: Whenever the owner is a person
मेरा भाई डाकघर में काम करता है uses मेरा because the owner (मैं) is not the subject.
Only with मैं and हम
अपना works with every subject: सीता अपने भाई के साथ बाज़ार जाती है.
items.why: If you can add “own” without changing the sense, use अपना (except in a joint subject).

items.q: Fill the gap: “The dog is under the bed.”
items.say: कुत्ता पलंग के नीचे है ।
wrong: की
की is used only with तरफ़ and तरह, which are feminine. नीचे takes के.
का
Compound postpositions begin with के, not का.
items.why: के नीचे “beneath, below”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Who is behind the door?”
items.say: दरवाज़े के पीछे कौन है ?
wrong: दरवाज़ा
A compound postposition takes the oblique, like a simple one: दरवाज़े.
दरवाज़ों
दरवाज़ों is plural. There is one door.
items.why: के पीछे “behind” needs the oblique case.

items.q: Fill the gap: “We go towards the station.”
items.say: हम स्टेशन की तरफ़ जाते हैं ।
wrong: के
तरफ़ is a feminine noun, so the postposition is की तरफ़.
का
Compound postpositions never begin with का. तरफ़ is feminine, so it is की तरफ़.
items.why: की तरफ़ “towards” and की तरह “like” use की.

items.q: Fill the gap: “This tea is for you. (to तुम)”
items.say: यह चाय तुम्हारे लिए है ।
items.en: This[0] tea[1] is[4] for[3] you[2]. (to तुम)
wrong: तुम के
With pronouns, compound postpositions are built on the possessive form. तुम्हारा gives तुम्हारे लिए.
तुम्हारी
लिए is preceded by के, so तुम्हारा becomes तुम्हारे.
items.why: मेरे लिए, तुम्हारे लिए, उसके लिए …

items.q: Fill the gap: “Mohan goes to the office with me.”
items.say: मोहन मेरे साथ दफ़्तर जाता है ।
items.en: Mohan[0] goes[4+5] {to the office}[3] with[2] me[1].
wrong: मुझ के
With pronouns, compound postpositions are built on the possessive form. मेरा gives मेरे साथ.
मेरी
साथ is preceded by के, so मेरा becomes मेरे.
items.why: के साथ “with”: मेरे साथ “with me”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Sita laughs like her mother.”
items.hi: सीता अपनी माँ ___ तरह हँसती है ।
items.say: सीता अपनी माँ की तरह हँसती है ।
wrong: के
तरह is a feminine noun, so it is की तरह.
का
Postpositions use की or के, never का.
items.why: की तरह “like”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “We go to Uncle's place on Fridays.”
items.hi: हम शुक्रवार को चाचा जी ___ यहाँ जाते हैं ।
items.say: हम शुक्रवार को चाचा जी के यहाँ जाते हैं ।
wrong: की
यहाँ is not a feminine noun. It is के यहाँ.
के यहाँ means “at the place of”. में cannot go before यहाँ.
items.why: के यहाँ “at someone's place (home)”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Please come before nine o'clock.”
items.say: नौ बजे से पहले आइए ।
wrong: की
पहले takes से or के, never की.
पर
पर means “on”. “Before” is से पहले.
items.why: पहले “before” can take से or के.

items.q: Fill the gap: “I often think about my village.”
items.hi: मैं अक्सर अपने गाँव ___ सोचता हूँ ।
items.say: मैं अक्सर अपने गाँव के बारे में सोचता हूँ ।
items.en: I[0] often[1] think[7+8] about[4+5+6] my[2] village[3].
wrong: के साथ
के साथ means “with”.
के लिए
के लिए means “for”.
items.why: के बारे में “about, concerning” has three words.

items.q: Fill the gap: “The post office is opposite the station.”
items.say: डाकघर स्टेशन के सामने है ।
items.en: {The post office}[0] is[4] opposite[2+3] the station[1].
wrong: पीछे
के पीछे means “behind”.
ऊपर
के ऊपर means “on top of”.
items.why: के सामने “facing, opposite”.

items.en: {The guests}[0] drink[4+5] tea[3] in[2] the garden[1].
wrong: पीता
मेहमान is plural here, as हैं shows, so the participle is पीते.
बग़ीचा
बग़ीचा is direct. Before में it is oblique: बग़ीचे.
हँसती
हँसना is “to laugh”. “To make laugh” is हँसाना, so हँसाती.
बच्चे
Before को the oblique plural is needed: बच्चों.

items.en: My[0] sister[1] is[5] sixteen[2] years[3] old[4].
wrong: का
का agrees with the subject, बहिन, which is feminine: की.
सालों
The sixteen years form one block of time, so साल is not made oblique plural.
उसके
उसके would be someone else's father. When the owner is the subject, Hindi uses अपना.
अपना
Before के पास the possessive is oblique: अपने.
आता
The verb agrees with संस्कृत, which is feminine: आती.
The verb agrees with संस्कृत, which is singular: है.

items.en: {The books}[0] are[4] {on top of}[2+3] the cupboard[1].
wrong: की
Only तरफ़ and तरह take की. ऊपर takes के.
है
किताबें is plural, so the verb is हैं.
बैठो
बैठो is the तुम command. आप takes बैठिए.
की
Only तरफ़ and तरह take की. नीचे takes के.
सोता
सोता is singular. बच्चे is plural.
सोना
सोना is the infinitive. The tense uses the participle.
कहता
The unstated subject is “they”, plural: कहते हैं.
बोलते
बोलना is “to speak”. “To call” is कहना.
हमारी
हमारी is feminine. कमरा is masculine.
हमारे
हमारे is plural or oblique. कमरा here is singular and direct.
items.order: यह हमारा कमरा है would mean “This is our room”. To say the room is ours, the possessive comes after the noun.

items.en: Their[0] friends[1] live[5+6] near[3+4] the station[2].
wrong: उनका
दोस्त is plural here, so उनका becomes उनके.
रहता
रहता is singular. The friends are several.
को
डरना marks what is feared with से.
कुत्ते
Before से the oblique plural is needed: कुत्तों.

lessons.title: What does it mean?
lessons.desc: Read a sentence, pick the translation

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: मेरे चाचा जी कभी नहीं हँसते ।
wrong: My uncle always laughs.
“Always” would be हमेशा. कभी नहीं is “never”.
My uncle sometimes laughs.
“Sometimes” would be कभी कभी.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: मेरे पति को संस्कृत नहीं आती ।
wrong: My husband doesn't like Sanskrit.
Liking is पसंद, as in मेरे पति को संस्कृत पसंद नहीं है.
My husband doesn't learn Sanskrit.
Learning is सीखना, as in मेरे पति संस्कृत नहीं सीखते.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: सीता अपनी सहेली के साथ स्कूल जाती है ।
items.a: Sita goes to school with her friend.
wrong: Sita's friend goes to school.
Sita is the subject, and के साथ means “with”.
Sita goes to her friend's school.
के साथ means “with”, not “of”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: मोहन उसकी गाड़ी में दफ़्तर जाता है ।
items.a: Mohan goes to the office in his (someone else's) car.
wrong: Mohan goes to the office in his own car.
“His own” would be अपनी गाड़ी. उसकी refers to someone other than the subject.
Mohan goes to his office by bus.
गाड़ी is a car; a bus would be बस.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: गाँवों में लोग जल्दी उठते हैं ।
items.a: In villages people get up early.
wrong: In the village people got up early.
उठते हैं is the imperfective present, a habit, not the past. गाँवों is plural.
In villages people go to bed early.
उठना is “to get up”. Going to bed would be सोना.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: मालूम होता है कि मालिक आज बीमार हैं ।
items.a: It seems the boss is ill today.
wrong: I know the boss is ill today.
“I know” would be मुझे मालूम है कि …. मालूम होता है means “it seems”.
The boss knows he is ill today.
मालिक is the subject of the second clause only. मालूम होता है means “it seems”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: हमारे दफ़्तर के पीछे एक बड़ा पेड़ है ।
items.a: There is a big tree behind our office.
wrong: There is a big tree in front of our office.
“In front of” is के आगे or के सामने. के पीछे is “behind”.
There is a big tree inside our office.
“Inside” is के अंदर.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: पिंकी हमेशा सब को हँसाती है ।
wrong: Pinki always laughs at everyone.
हँसाना is “to make laugh”. Laughing is हँसना, as in हँसती.
Pinki never makes anyone laugh.
हमेशा means “always”. “Never” is कभी नहीं.

items.q: When can हूँ, है, हो or हैं be dropped after the participle?
wrong: In questions
Questions keep the auxiliary: तुम रात को क्या पढ़ते हो ?
Whenever the subject is plural
Plural subjects keep हैं, as in बच्चे बग़ीचे में खेलते हैं.
items.why: After नहीं the auxiliary is often left out: मोहन दफ़्तर नहीं जाता.

items.q: What does the imperfective present describe?
items.a: Habits and regular events, and ongoing states of mind
wrong: An action going on right now, like “he is speaking”
Continuous actions have a separate tense, taught in Unit 8.
A single event in the past
The past of होना is था. This tense is present.
items.why: बोलता है “speaks” (habitually); सोचता है “thinks”.

items.q: How are compound postpositions used with pronouns?
items.a: With the possessive form: मेरे लिए, उसके साथ
wrong: With the direct pronoun: मैं के लिए
A postposition never follows a direct pronoun. With pronouns, compound postpositions are built on the possessive form.
With the oblique pronoun: मुझ के लिए
With pronouns, compound postpositions are built on the possessive form. मेरा gives मेरे लिए.
items.why: मेरा → मेरे लिए, हमारा → हमारी तरफ़, अपना → अपने बारे में.

items.q: Which word is the grammatical subject of उसे ज़ुकाम है ?
wrong: उसे
उसे is उस को. A word followed by को is never the subject: the subject must be in the direct case.
है
है is the verb.
items.why: In the को construction the thing (here ज़ुकाम) is the subject, and the person takes को.

items.q: Why do की तरफ़ and की तरह use की ?
items.a: Because those two nouns are feminine
wrong: Because the noun before them is feminine
The noun before does not matter: बहिन के साथ, घर की तरफ़. Only तरफ़ and तरह make it की.
Because the postposition means “towards”
की is the feminine form of का. तरफ़ is a noun meaning “direction”.
items.why: Other compound postpositions begin with के.
